question: Should agent-behavior governance become a permanent core `security.behaviorPolicy` contract, or remain an optional plugin built on the existing typed policy hooks?
rationale: This choice defines a new security and configuration promise plus a competing enforcement owner; implementation review cannot decide whether prompt guidance and external validation should be represented as a core security boundary.

options.title: Use the plugin policy surface
options.body: Keep core lean, implement the feature with existing typed hooks, and add only a narrowly proven missing SDK capability if necessary.

options.title: Sponsor a core contract
options.body: Explicitly accept the new core surface, then require complete schema and upgrade semantics, deterministic enforcement placement, failure policy, documentation, and live proof.

options.title: Pause the proposal
options.body: Close or defer the PR until a concrete workflow demonstrates a security-policy gap that current plugin hooks cannot safely cover.

recommendation.title: Use the plugin policy surface
recommendation.body: Keep core lean, implement the feature with existing typed hooks, and add only a narrowly proven missing SDK capability if necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans OpenClaw product scope, core configuration, plugin architecture, and the documented security model.
